text: A robot arm with three or more rotary joints, such as the common six-axis industrial arm. Industrial arms are usually programmed with a teach pendant (a handheld control panel) or by offline programming in simulation on a PC.

evidence.quote: Industrial arms are usually programmed with a teach pendant (a handheld control panel) or by offline programming in simulation on a PC.

text: An optional part of a UR PolyScope program runs once before the main program loop. It is used to put the robot and tools in a known state. For example, this sequence is used to avoid collisions or bumps when a program starts again after the previous run has ended.

evidence.quote: avoid collisions or bumps when a program starts again after the previous run has ended

text: The rate at which a PWM square wave completes full ON/OFF cycles, measured in Hertz (Hz). Carrier frequencies of 490 Hz and 980 Hz sit well inside the audible range.

evidence.quote: Carrier frequencies of 490 Hz and 980 Hz sit well inside the audible range.

text: A technique that uses a polarizer on the light source and an analyzer on the camera lens eliminates direct specular glare from reflective surfaces. The polarizer and analyzer are oriented at 90 degrees to each other.

A non-linear adaptation of the Kalman filter that linearizes dynamic and measurement functions locally around the current state estimate. It calculates these linear approximations using Jacobian matrices from a first-order Taylor series.
A system design pattern where a robot stays in exactly one state at a time. The system switches between defined states when specific sensor events or conditions occur.

A ros2_control plugin connects controllers to a specific robot, real or simulated. It reads joint states from the robot and writes commands to it, so the controllers above it do not need to know the brand.

The difference (residual) between an actual sensor measurement and the measurement predicted by the system state model. A filter ignores a sensor reading whose innovation is too large compared with the predicted uncertainty.

evidence.quote: ignores a sensor reading whose innovation is too large compared with the predicted uncertainty

text: A ros2_control controller that accepts FollowJointTrajectory goals and moves a group of joints through timed waypoints. It executes trajectories by interpolating in time between waypoints that hold positions and optional velocities and accelerations.

evidence.quote: interpolating in time between waypoints that hold positions and optional velocities and accelerations

text: A modern container file format designed specifically for robotics telemetry and multimodal sensor logging in ros2 bag. It gives fast, efficient reading so tools can jump to a point in a recording without reading the whole file.

evidence.quote: fast, efficient reading, so tools can jump to a point in a recording without reading the whole file

text: The ROS 2 driver from Yaskawa runs on the robot controller as a MotoPlus application. It connects to ROS 2 through a micro-ROS Agent running on the PC.
A name prefix, such as /turtlesim1, is added to a node's name and its relative topic names. This prefix lets identical nodes run side by side without conflicts.
A method that involves writing and testing a robot program on a computer in 3D simulation. The real robot can keep working until the finished program is downloaded to it.

An optical lens aberration where magnification increases toward the periphery, pulling straight lines outward from the center. This distortion misplaces points without blurring them, so it can be calibrated and corrected in software.

evidence.quote: distortion misplaces points without blurring them, toward the center (barrel) or away from it (pincushion), so it can be calibrated and corrected in software

text: Maintenance that is scheduled, timed, or based on an operating cycle. The work is done on schedule whether or not the machine shows a problem.

evidence.quote: The work is done on schedule whether or not the machine shows a problem.

text: A strongly typed, multitasking procedural programming language from ABB used across IRC5 and OmniCore robot controllers. A single RAPID motion instruction names its target, its speed, its zone, and its tool.

evidence.quote: A single RAPID motion instruction names its target, its speed, its zone, and its tool

text: A Linux kernel built or tuned (for example PREEMPT_RT or low-latency) runs tasks with predictable timing. This lets time-critical tasks such as a 500 Hz robot control loop meet their deadlines.
A machine that senses its surroundings, decides what to do with a program, and acts on the world. An example is an industrial robot, such as a six-axis arm guided by a program on an assembly line.
The fixed interval at which a digital controller reads its sensor and updates its output. For example, it is 100 ms in the Arduino PID Library by default.
The target value a controller tries to reach, such as a desired speed or position. For motion control, a ramped setpoint is gentler on mechanics than a step.

evidence.quote: a ramped setpoint is gentler on mechanics than a step

text: The taught robot pose from which a wrist-mounted camera takes its pictures. The robot must stop at the snapshot position before every picture, and the result depends on the robot reaching that pose repeatably.

evidence.quote: the robot must stop at the snapshot position before every picture, and the result depends on the robot reaching that pose repeatably

text: A reactive control design created by Rodney Brooks in 1986 stacks simple behaviors in layers. Under this design, higher layers can suppress the outputs of lower ones while the lower layers keep running.

The ROS 2 library that keeps track of coordinate frames and the transforms between them over time. In Nav2, the robot must build a transform tree with the full chain: map, odom, base_link, then its sensor frames.

evidence.quote: build a transform tree with the full chain: map, odom, base_link, then its sensor frames

text: The RAPID data type defines a tool mounted on the robot. It describes whether the robot holds it, its TCP frame, and its load (mass, center of gravity and inertia).
The first industrial robot was developed by George Devol and Joseph Engelberger. In 1961, it began handling hot die-cast parts at a General Motors plant in New Jersey.

Driving to a list of destinations in turn, optionally doing a task at each one. In Nav2, the software has a plugin interface for a task at each one, such as taking a picture, picking up a box or waiting for user input.

evidence.quote: sends the robot to several destinations and has a plugin interface for a task at each one, such as taking a picture, picking up a box or waiting for user input

text: How an industrial arm is built: joints, degrees of freedom, the work envelope, coordinate frames, and the tool center point. It also explains how a controller interpolates joint and straight-line moves.
Plan and execute arm motions with MoveIt 2 on ROS 2 Lyrical. The lesson covers URDF and SRDF, ros2_control mock hardware, move_group, OMPL and Pilz PTP/LIN, and a UR5e in RViz.

Core 2D image processing: color space conversion, histograms and contrast equalization, and global, Otsu and adaptive thresholding. The lesson also covers contours, moments, blobs, Canny edge detection, and template matching.

Lab: the UR Modbus TCP server and its general-purpose registers, including packing handshake bits in URScript. Connect from Python with pymodbus to write and read registers (stand-in server, no hardware).
